One-sentence judgment: farm products buyers do not just go to the market to buy vegetables, but purchase agricultural products such as milk, grain, and Christmas trees for further processing or resale, and are responsible for price, contract terms, quality grading, transport and storage, and transaction records. O*NET lists this occupation as Job Zone Four (considerable preparation needed, SVP 7.0 to below 8.0), marks Bright Outlook, and gives interest code ECR (enterprising, conventional, realistic). The core boundary is: you can review orders, negotiate contracts with farmers, inspect and grade, arrange transport and storage, and maintain transaction records; but you cannot replace inspection and quarantine or food safety regulatory judgment, you cannot decide the enterprise's funding and credit limits on your own, and you cannot commit to purchases externally while bypassing authorization and compliance processes.

Signals for continued exploration: you are willing to negotiate with numbers and terms and write the agreement clearly; you can make judgments and document them when yield and price are uncertain; you are willing to check orders, inventory, and transport records item by item; you have a basic interest in crops, livestock and poultry, seasons, and the cold chain; you can align repeatedly among farmers, carriers, processors, and internal departments; and you accept a daily work style dominated by data checking, document handling, and negotiation and communication.

Conditions for pausing high-cost investment first: you have not yet completed one full closed loop from demand review, price inquiry and contract points, quality and grading, transport and storage, to documented records; or you are unwilling to check prices and contract terms through process and only want to negotiate by feel; and do not treat being good at bargaining or knowing agriculture as proof that you can independently carry purchasing commitments and contract responsibility.

Education, qualifications, and authorization must be checked separately: O*NET lists this occupation as Job Zone Four (considerable preparation needed, SVP 7.0 to below 8.0), and most positions require a four-year bachelor's degree, while some accept a high school diploma or equivalent together with related experience and on-the-job training. In the United States, position requirements are set by the employer, and this occupation usually has no unified individual practice license; in mainland China, the Occupational Classification Compendium of the People's Republic of China (2022 edition) has no detailed category corresponding one-to-one with this entry, and the related duties may fall under purchasing, agricultural product brokerage, and supply chain positions, which must be judged by the actual duties of the position. Education, industry knowledge, negotiation authorization, and contract signing authority are four different things and cannot substitute for one another.

In one sentence: this is a role responsible for the price, contracts, quality, and records of agricultural product purchasing, with outputs of purchase contracts and orders, quality and grading determinations, transport and storage arrangements, and inventory and transaction records; it is not an inspection and quarantine regulatory role and does not replace the enterprise's funding and compliance decisions. US wage and employment data are labeled on the O*NET page as the parent occupation Buyers and Purchasing Agents basis, and this page presents them on that proxy basis; for mainland China, under the evidence route only the statistical basis and gaps are registered, with no occupation-level values published and no industry average used to fill them in.

The work of this occupation falls into three categories: first, purchasing and negotiation (reviewing orders and demand, price inquiry and bargaining, negotiating production or purchase contracts with farmers, and setting variety and quantity); second, quality and grading (inspecting or testing crops and products, estimating value and grade, and looking at fields and production conditions); third, logistics and records (arranging transport and storage, coordinating processing or resale, and maintaining transaction and inventory records and reporting as needed). All three share the same chain centered on price, contracts, and traceable records.
Purchasing and negotiation

Review orders and demand → inquire about prices and compare quotes → negotiate production or purchase contracts with farmers → set variety, quantity, and delivery conditions → form the contract and order → record and hand over to the execution stage.
Quality and grading

Look at fields and production conditions → inspect or test crops and products → estimate value and determine grade → identify disease, pests, or quality anomalies → form acceptance and grading records → escalate anomalies through procedure.

Arrange transport or storage → coordinate cutting, transport, storage, or milling stages → maintain business transaction and product inventory records → report data to the company or government agencies as needed → recheck transport and storage conditions → complete handover and documentation.

Editorial duty comparison: farm products purchasing differs from purchasing management, supply chain, farm operation, non-agricultural purchasing, other purchasing agents, and grading and sorting in object and training, and managers may also take part in individual negotiations, so positions may overlap; exclusive duties are not asserted from the name, and authorization is still checked against real rules.
Core purpose

Obtain agricultural products steadily for processing or resale under controllable price, quality, and delivery conditions: lock quantity and conditions with contracts and orders, control quality with inspection and grading, and make the process traceable with transport and storage arrangements and transaction records.
Main objects and basis

The objects are agricultural products such as milk, grain, Christmas trees, and tobacco, farmers and producers, orders and demand plans, transport and storage stages, acceptance and grading standards, and business transaction and inventory records; the basis is purchasing policy and authorized limits, contract terms and payment conditions, quality standards and grading rules, transport and storage requirements, record and reporting rules, and the organization's compliance and conflict of interest rules.
Core process

Review orders and demand, inquire and bargain, negotiate and sign contracts, inspect and grade, arrange transport and storage, maintain transaction and inventory records, and escalate anomalies and hand over.
Main outputs

Purchase contracts and orders, supplier and farmer communication records, quality and grading determinations, transport and storage arrangements, business transaction and product inventory records, and reports submitted to the company or government agencies as needed.
Responsible parties

Editorial division check: confirm with the enterprise the actual responsibilities and approval paths of purchasing, finance, quality, logistics, and management, without specifying the same division for all organizations; acceptance and regulatory inspection and quarantine conclusions are kept separate.
Authority and approval

Editorial permission check: price inquiry, external commitments, contracts, quality acceptance, payment, and related-party transactions are checked separately against real authorization and applicable rules; this page does not determine the validity of external contracts and does not grant approval authority on the basis of experience or connections.
Conclusion boundaries

Purchase price and contract records state what agreement was reached under the given quality standards, delivery conditions, and scope of authorization; they are not a food safety or inspection and quarantine conclusion and do not replace the enterprise's funding and compliance decisions, and they are updated as season, yield, market, and contract terms change; the variety, batch, and date should be stated when citing them.

Before starting, check at least six items: position duties (leaning toward category purchasing, contracts and brokerage, or quality and logistics), authorized limits and the approval chain, review basis (price, shrinkage, delivery achievement, or inventory turnover), quality and acceptance standards, transport and storage conditions, and conflict of interest and compliance declaration requirements.
Occupation basis

O*NET13-1021 farm products purchasing, ZoneFour/SVP7 to below 8, BrightOutlook. The 2025 parent occupation 13-1020 industry is 22% manufacturing, 14% wholesale, 13% government, and 51% other (including enterprise management and professional, scientific, and technical services), not the precise distribution of the farm products detailed category. O*NET interest ECR: E65/C63/R59/I14/S12/A1 are the six types; the 41 specific interest areas are scored independently, with agriculture 58, management and administration 47, accounting 44, and entrepreneurship 39, which are not exclusive subcategories of E/C/R or an individual ability threshold. The one-to-one mapping between the China 2022 occupation classification detailed categories and US 13-1021 was not completed this round; check against real purchasing duties, and a publication entry point cannot prove that no corresponding detailed category exists.
Education and training paths

O*NET new entrant education Q&A for farm products purchasing lists a bachelor's degree, high school or equivalent, and a non-degree postsecondary certificate as required for some positions, and this page does not show percentages; this is not the incumbent education composition; ZoneFour/SVP7 to below 8 is the broad preparation level. The BLS parent occupation 13-1020 typical is a bachelor's degree, related experience None, and moderate-term OJT, and the OOH states that buyers usually train for several months and that some positions accept high school; the years of experience required of managers cannot be applied to buyers. In China, Article 9 of the 2021 Regulations on the Administration of Grain Circulation as read requires grain purchasing enterprises to file with the locality of purchase, and Articles 10 to 14 set price and quality standards, fair pricing by quality, timely payment, quality inspection, and reporting, storage, and transport requirements; these are limited to the grain category and are not a unified individual qualification for all agricultural products. The US USDA states that certain fresh and frozen fruit and vegetable businesses may require a PACA license, and the business, the transaction parties, and the threshold are checked separately and not applied broadly to grain, milk, or tobacco or to every employed person. Enterprise business qualification, individual certification, and contract authorization are kept separate; this round did not complete the check of all categories and local regulations, and it is not claimed that both places have uniformly no license.

The detailed profile has 14 software categories; 2025 hiring hot technology has 13 products and 7 InDemand. Excel29%, Office24%, Outlook11%, Word, SAP, and PowerPoint 6% each, and Access1%, with the remaining 6 products NA and not 0; purchasing software is another InDemand item, and the 13 hot products must not be treated as all software categories. Pay and working hours

O*NET97% have a regular schedule, 84% work more than 40 hours per week, and 16% exactly 40; it is not presumed that every position necessarily works overtime or travels during harvest season. Precise occupational wage evidence for farm products purchasing in China is insufficient. NBS2025 industry references: manufacturing non-private 113594 / private 76055, and wholesale and retail non-private 135749 / private 69622 yuan pre-tax annual average (Tables 2 and 5). They serve respectively as industry background references for raw material purchasing for processing or trade purchasing, mix multiple occupations, and are not the median, starting pay, city monthly salary, or a personal offer for farm products purchasing, and cannot automatically cover individual brokers. The editorial suggestion is to check authorization, review, travel, season, and the pay contract.

Farm products buyers (O*NET-SOC 13-1021.00, Buyers and Purchasing Agents, Farm Products) purchase farm products for further processing or resale, including tree farm contractors, grain brokers and market operators, grain buyers, and tobacco buyers, and may need to negotiate contracts. Daily work includes: purchasing agricultural products such as milk, grain, and Christmas trees for further processing or resale; negotiating agricultural product production or purchase contracts with farmers; maintaining business transaction and product inventory records and reporting data to the company or government agencies as needed; reviewing orders to determine the product type and quantity needed to meet demand; arranging transport or storage of purchased products; coordinating or directing workers engaged in cutting, transport, storage, or milling and in maintaining records; arranging processing or resale of purchased products; inspecting or testing crops and products to estimate value, determine grade, or find disease and pests; and estimating land production potential, looking at fields, and studying factors such as crop rotation history, soil fertility, or irrigation facilities. It carries responsibility for price and contracts, quality and grading, transport and storage, and transaction records, but does not replace inspection and quarantine, food safety regulation, or the enterprise's funding and compliance decisions.

paragraphs: This page compares farm products buyers with five adjacent directions on the same set of dimensions: occupational direction, core work and outputs, key differences, and which direction each preference suits better. Adjacent directions are described according to their own official occupational descriptions, and this does not mean position titles are interchangeable.

Evidence note: occupational directions and core outputs are based on the official descriptions of O*NET 13-1021.00 and the adjacent entries (US basis); authorized limits, contract signing authority, quality determination authority, and compliance requirements must be verified separately for each organization and jurisdiction, and this page does not present any direction as a shortcut to a career change.

The table below compares farm products buyers with adjacent directions in duties and outputs; the judgment is based on main outputs, responsibility objects, and required authorization, not on how similar the position titles are.

Purchasing managers own the budget and team and are responsible for departmental results and do not take on the bargaining and grading of individual agricultural product transactions; this occupation completes single price inquiries, negotiations, and acceptance within authorized limits and honestly records price and quality conclusions.

If you would rather be responsible for strategy, budget, and the team, look first at the purchasing manager direction; if you would rather negotiate individual agricultural product purchases yourself, look first at this occupation.
Be responsible for the purchasing department's goals, budget, team, and supplier strategy, with outputs mainly rules, metrics, and team management.
Purchasing managers (Purchasing Managers)

Supply chain managers focus on planning and inventory efficiency across the chain, and their work is mainly systems and processes; this occupation focuses on the price, quality, and delivery of specific varieties, and the work is mainly individual transactions and on-site determinations.

If you would rather do planning system and process design, look first at the supply chain manager direction; if you would rather do variety purchasing and on-site determinations, look first at this occupation.
Design end-to-end planning, inventory, and processes, with outputs mainly the planning system, turnover metrics, and process improvement.
Supply chain managers (Supply Chain Managers)

Farmers and agricultural managers are the operators on the production side and earn from production and sales, and in role terms they are often the counterparty of this occupation; this occupation negotiates on the buyer's side and carries purchasing cost and quality responsibility and does not take on production arrangements.

If you would rather organize production and work the land, look first at the agricultural manager direction; if you would rather negotiate and accept goods on the buyer's side, look first at this occupation.
Organize agricultural and livestock production and operation, with outputs mainly output volume, cost, and production plans.
Farmers, ranchers, and other agricultural managers (Farmers, Ranchers, and Other Agricultural Managers)

That category of buyer deals with industrial and consumer goods and focuses on sales and turnover; this occupation deals with agricultural products and focuses on season, yield, quality, and grading, and more often involves contracts and transport and storage.

If you would rather do consumer goods categories and store replenishment, look first at the wholesale and retail buyer direction; if you would rather handle agricultural products and negotiate with producers, look first at this occupation.
Purchase and replenish non-agricultural categories, with outputs mainly category structure, gross margin, and inventory turnover.
Wholesale and retail buyers, except farm products (Wholesale and Retail Buyers, Except Farm Products)

That category of purchasing agent deals with equipment, materials, and services, and its processes and compliance requirements are closer to internal procurement; this occupation deals with agricultural products and producers, with a higher share of price fluctuation, quality grading, and transport and storage.

If you would rather do equipment and materials and internal procurement, look first at the other purchasing agent direction; if you would rather do agricultural products and on-site field determinations, look first at this occupation.
Purchase equipment, materials, and services on behalf of the organization, with outputs mainly procurement plans, cost savings, and compliance records.
Purchasing agents, except wholesale, retail, and farm products (Purchasing Agents, Except Wholesale, Retail, and Farm Products)

Graders and sorters grade to established standards and do not take part in bargaining or contracts; this occupation's grading determinations serve purchasing decisions and it is also responsible for price and contract terms.

If you would rather do grading and sorting to standard, look first at the agricultural product grader and sorter direction; if you would rather link the determination to price and contracts, look first at this occupation.
Grade and sort agricultural products to standard, with outputs mainly grading results and batch records.
Graders and sorters, agricultural products (Graders and Sorters, Agricultural Products)

Conclusion: the choice of direction is based on main outputs, responsibility objects, and required authorization, not on how similar the names are; once a direction is chosen, check item by item the target position's authorized limits, approval chain, review basis, quality and acceptance standards, and travel and purchasing season arrangements, and keep written confirmation.

paragraphs: Students or career changers preparing to enter this occupation

First complete one closed loop with public or simulated materials: turn one requirement into price inquiry points, do one price and terms comparison, write out the basis for quality and grading determinations, then design the transport and storage arrangements, and finally have a practitioner point out contract and compliance problems; at the same time check the target position's authorized limits and approval chain.
Practicing farm products buyers

Editorial process check: use tools for reviewable steps such as market information organization, generating price comparison tables, drafting contract points, and record aggregation; price judgments, contract commitments, acceptance and grading conclusions, and authorization and compliance determinations must still be checked and documented by the buyer.
Purchasing and supply chain management positions

Editorial process check: before introducing automatic price comparison or market forecasting tools, first clarify the data sources and update timing, how exceptions are handled, who reviews quotes and inventory, and how approvals and documentation are retained, so that any automatic result can be checked against the contract, order, and actual inventory, and human responsibility for authorization and compliance is retained.
Training and mentoring

Focus training on category knowledge, price inquiry and bargaining, contract terms, quality and grading, and transport, storage, and reporting; also train the habit of checking automatically generated price comparisons and summaries, especially data sources, timing, and basis.

entries.answer: Purchase agricultural products such as milk, grain, and Christmas trees for further processing or resale: review orders and demand, inquire and compare quotes, negotiate production or purchase contracts with farmers, inspect or test crops and products to estimate value, determine grade, or find disease and pests, arrange transport or storage of purchased products, coordinate cutting, transport, storage, or milling stages, arrange processing or resale, and maintain business transaction and product inventory records and report data to the company or government agencies as needed.
entries.question: What do farm products buyers do every day?

entries.answer: The main risks are wrong commitments from misjudged market information and quotes, cost and disputes from incomplete contract terms, acceptance disputes and downstream losses from deviations in quality and grading determinations, shrinkage in the transport and storage stage, incomplete transaction and inventory records, and exceeding authorized limits or failing to declare conflicts of interest; controls rely on checking sources and timing, fixing contract terms, inspecting and grading to standard, rechecking transport and storage conditions, retaining records, and a clear authorization, approval, and declaration and recusal process.
entries.question: What risks most need attention in advance in this job?

entries.answer: Fit signals are being able to read market information and quotes and check them item by item, being willing to write contract terms and quality conditions clearly, and being able to restrain commitments within authorization and compliance boundaries; being good at bargaining or knowing agriculture is not enough to prove competence, and what matters is whether there are reviewable price comparison and contract records, acceptance and grading records, and compliance documentation.

subject.name: Farm products buyers
subject.summary: The entries on this page correspond to farm products buyers (O*NET-SOC 13-1021.00, Buyers and Purchasing Agents, Farm Products): purchasing agricultural products such as milk, grain, and Christmas trees for further processing or resale — reviewing orders and demand, inquiring and bargaining, negotiating contracts with farmers, inspecting and grading, arranging transport and storage, coordinating processing or resale, and maintaining business transaction and inventory records and reporting as needed; the work is mainly data checking and contract and document handling (100% take part in face-to-face discussions every day, 100% use email every day, 76% sit continuously, and 71% say being accurate is extremely important), and its duties do not equal inspection and quarantine or food safety regulation, nor do they replace the enterprise's funding and compliance decisions.
